text: It is urged that the unique characteristics of freight forwarding compel a different delimitation of terminal areas than that accorded motor carriers. The freight forwarders presented evidence relating to several problems peculiar to their industry and the need for large terminal areas for collection and delivery. A fundamental problem has been the migration of shippers to locations in industrial parks beyond present terminal area limits. In Ex Parte No. 266 (Sub-No. 1), the forwarders presented evidence compiled by a research and consulting firm documenting actual shipper relocations. In this proceeding the forwarders rely on a similar presentation demonstrating demographic trends. We believe that the revised population-mileage formula adopted herein should remedy this problem to a great extent. Based on the evidence of record, including that presented by the freight forwarders, and the assessment of our Bureau of Economics, we have attempted to devise a formula which encompasses most suburban shippers and industrial parks. The expanded formula distances take in an area which is within reasonable geographic proximity to the central city and shares a commercial relationship with it. Many factors, including the extent of modern transportation networks, have entered into our consideration. Therefore, we feel that the revised population-mileage formula meets a basic need of the freight forwarder industry and adequately covers the geographic extent of "'local' movements of traffic" within areas having "a logical geographic relationship to each other." See, Freight Forwarder Institute v. United States, 409 F. Supp. at 707.
